q: How much of a printing press's electricity goes to UV curing?
title: Printing presses: UV curing electricity
short: Measure it: put a meter on the UV lamp supply for a week of normal jobs and compare with the press total. On presses that cure every unit with mercury lamps it is often a large share, and LED curing cuts it sharply.
audience: Commercial, label and packaging printers running UV or LED UV presses

ol: Clamp or install a meter on the UV power supply.
Log kWh with press hours and impressions for a representative week.
Divide lamp kWh by total press kWh to get the share, and by impressions to get kWh per thousand.

p: Lamp hours on idle, lamps left at full power between jobs, and ageing reflectors are common waste. A before and after reading is the evidence for a retrofit to LED.
It is all Scope 2 electricity at 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25. The share tells you where a saving would come from.

example.title: Illustrative week on one press
lines: Press total: 4,200 kWh; UV lamps: 1,900 kWh, a 45% share
example.note: Figures are illustrative; your own meter readings decide the share.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and diesel, LPG and gas invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a dated, fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record for each site. Intensity per unit uses the activity count you enter, and estimates are labelled as estimates.
